findings.evidence: The document uses three different terms for the same concept: 'equipment' (line 45: 'keep the equipment in good working condition'), 'device' (line 47: 'one device per category'), and 'stipend item' (lines 50-52: 'stipend item on the request form'). All three refer to the purchased item the employee is requesting reimbursement for.
findings.fix: Select one primary term and use it consistently throughout the document (recommend 'equipment'). If the document must use alternate terms in specific contexts, add an explicit note in the Terminology section stating the equivalences, such as: 'Equipment, device, and stipend item refer to the same purchased item throughout this policy.'
findings.location: Throughout document: Eligibility (line 11), Restrictions and Exceptions (line 47), Terminology Notes (lines 50-52)
findings.violation: The reader cannot determine whether these three terms name identical items or three different artifacts. The interchangeable use without definition forces the reader to check whether 'device' is a subset of 'equipment' or a synonym for 'stipend item', creating unnecessary cognitive load.

findings.evidence: The finance office conducts an evaluation of every submitted receipt before it approves the amount.

findings.evidence: The Required Documentation section appears after the Approval Timeline section. A reader applying for the stipend would need to know what documentation is required before or immediately after learning how to apply, not after learning about the approval timeline. The Reimbursement Amounts section also appears late, after the reader has already learned about the application process.
findings.fix: Reorder sections to place Required Documentation immediately after 'How to Apply' and before 'Approval Timeline'. Move Reimbursement Amounts earlier, ideally before or right after Eligibility, so readers know both who qualifies and how much the benefit is worth.
findings.location: Document structure: Required Documentation section (section 5) and Reimbursement Amounts section (section 6)
findings.violation: The section order follows an internal workflow (how the organization processes requests) rather than the reader's actual task sequence (what do I need to prepare, how do I submit, what happens next). Readers must re-read or skip ahead to learn essential preparation information.
